newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - NOV 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - NOV 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Anglovaal's gold division, Avgold, has launched itself on the international stage as a focused company with its long-term resources secured and the mines' frequently criticised management contracts at an end.

- First National Bank lifted attributable earnings a disappointing 15.6 percent to one billion rand for the year to September, after a sharp increase in bad debts arising mainly from consumer-related instalment credit and private label card activities.
- South Africa's government suspended its 80 million rand arms deal with the Rwandan government yesterday as a result of allegations that Rwandan troops were conducting cross-border raids into Zaire.

- The National Party admitted it had an "image" problem with the credibility of former NP cabinets in the light of allegations linking atrocities to former NP ministers, party secretary-general Roelf Meyer said yesterday.
- Foreign exchange outflows have triggered increases in money market interest rates and put pressure on banks' margins as they scramble for cash.

- The Independent Broadcasting Authority conceded in the Rand Supreme Court yesterday that its council had not had a quorum when it decided on the successful bidder for Radio Jacaranda's broadcast licence.
- South African Airways said yesterday it had been the victim of industrial espionage in which sensitive information was passed to a European competitor.

- San Vito Development , which is listed under the property sector and which has been resuscitated recently after a two-year Johannesburg Stock Exchange suspension, has moved into the leisure industry by acquiring joint control in the Musselcracker restaurant group and Bertie's Landing, the popular Cape waterfront venue.

- Stella Sigcau, the public enterprises minister, has recommended to the Cabinet that Sipho Nyawo, the executive director of Portnet, be dismissed because of an investigation into alleged credit card abuse, Wandile Zote, a ministerial spokesman, said last night.
- Illovo Sugar is to invest about 90 million rand in rehabilitating a Mozambican sugar mill in line with its expansion drive into Africa, Don MacLeod, Illovo's managing director, said yesterday.

- The South African government is hurriedly preparing plans to contribute personnel, logistics and equipment -- but probably not combat troops -- to support an international peace-keeping force to intervene in the conflict in Zaire, if asked to by the United Nations.

- There was confusion and contradiction yesterday when Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi said in parliament that almost 1,000 motor vehicles were being hijacked every month in Gauteng and vehicle hijacking countrywide had more than doubled since the start of the year.
But Mufamadi's spokesman, Maxwell Malaudzi, said last night that these figures were incorrect and new figures would be released today.

- Aids lobby groups and doctors in South Africa have called for the government to subsidise newly available Aids "cocktail" therapies -- a combination of drugs that are said to knock out the virus and are having dramatic effects overseas.
